pr_title: Fix “Authorized applications” inefficiently and incorrectly getting last use date
pr_body:
Fixes #20477

Thanks @renchap for writing the more efficient query.

issue_context.title: "Authorized applications" in settings takes 18.6 seconds to load
issue_context.body:
### Steps to reproduce the problem

Go to Settings > Account > Authorized applications

### Expected behaviour

it loads quickly

### Actual behaviour

it loads very slowly (18.6s)

### Detailed description

_No response_

### Specifications

mastodon.social
comments: I can't reproduce it, but how many registered apps do you have?
There's at least one N+1 when doing `most_recently_used_access_token`
Somewhere in the neighborhood of about ~130 or so? It's a lot.

Update: this page load now results in a complete failure. I have no idea how many authorized applications I have, and I am actually completely unable to revoke any of them or do any sort of management on them. Which seems... problematic, to say the least...

I just checked, 114 applications at the moment on this specific account

`Doorkeeper.config.application_model.authorized_for(user)` is fast for your account, so I guess there is a N+1 query somewhere, triggered by the view.
I have a test account on mastodon.social that easily has a thousand logins and https://mastodon.social/oauth/authorized_applications returns 503.

There is indeed a N+1 in the view, `most_recently_used_access_token` is called for every application and is very inefficient (not using an index…).
It may also be wrong, as an app could be used by multiple users, and it does not select access tokens for the current user only.

The most recently used token's last usage date can be fetched for all apps at once, using a query like:
```ruby
last_used_at_by_app = Doorkeeper::AccessToken
  .select('DISTINCT ON (application_id) application_id, last_used_at')
  .where(resource_owner_id: current_user.id)
  .where.not(last_used_at: nil)
  .order(application_id: :desc, last_used_at: :desc)
  .pluck(:application_id, :last_used_at)
  .to_h
```

This query takes < 1ms for OP's account on mastodon.social.

review_comments:
I realize this is more than a year old, but bumped into this looking at something else. In this query, this line (the `DISTINCT` portion) doesnt actually come through in the generated sql.

I think what happens is the `pluck` overwrites the `select` line here, so the distinct portion of query gets dropped ... but then also, the final `to_h` essentially does what we want in terms of preparing a hash with unique keys (application IDs) each pointing to a datetime value for the view where this is used to consume.

That said, I'm not sure that the correct time gets picked. Example here...

```
mastodon(dev)>     @last_used_at_by_app = Doorkeeper::AccessToken
mastodon(dev)>                            .select('DISTINCT ON (application_id) application_id, last_used_at')
mastodon(dev)>                            .where(resource_owner_id: current_resource_owner.id)
mastodon(dev)>                            .where.not(last_used_at: nil)
mastodon(dev)>                            .order(application_id: :desc, last_used_at: :desc)
mastodon(dev)>                            .pluck(:application_id, :last_used_at)
mastodon(dev)>                            .to_h
mastodon(dev)> 
  Doorkeeper::AccessToken Pluck (0.2ms)  SELECT "oauth_access_tokens"."application_id", "oauth_access_tokens"."last_used_at" FROM "oauth_access_tokens" WHERE "oauth_access_tokens"."resource_owner_id" = $1 AND "oauth_access_tokens"."last_used_at" IS NOT NULL ORDER BY "oauth_access_tokens"."application_id" DESC, "oauth_access_tokens"."last_used_at" DESC  [["resource_owner_id", 3]]
=> {3=>Sat, 09 Nov 2024 17:46:10.071951000 UTC +00:00}
mastodon(dev)>     @last_used_at_by_app = Doorkeeper::AccessToken
mastodon(dev)>                            .select('DISTINCT ON (application_id) application_id, last_used_at')
mastodon(dev)>                            .where(resource_owner_id: current_resource_owner.id)
mastodon(dev)>                            .where.not(last_used_at: nil)
mastodon(dev)>                            .order(application_id: :desc, last_used_at: :desc)
mastodon(dev)>                            .pluck(:application_id, :last_used_at)
mastodon(dev)> 
  Doorkeeper::AccessToken Pluck (0.2ms)  SELECT "oauth_access_tokens"."application_id", "oauth_access_tokens"."last_used_at" FROM "oauth_access_tokens" WHERE "oauth_access_tokens"."resource_owner_id" = $1 AND "oauth_access_tokens"."last_used_at" IS NOT NULL ORDER BY "oauth_access_tokens"."application_id" DESC, "oauth_access_tokens"."last_used_at" DESC  [["resource_owner_id", 3]]
=> [[3, Thu, 14 Nov 2024 17:38:12.812377000 UTC +00:00], [3, Sat, 09 Nov 2024 17:46:10.071951000 UTC +00:00]]
```

Note how the first one (copied straight from here, including final `to_h`) does get us a uniquely-keyed hash, the second one (exact same, drops final `to_h`) shows the two values we could have chosen. Presumably we would have wanted the latter (11-14 in this example, not 11-09) value to be chosen?

If I remove the `pluck` line, the DISTINCT bit does run, and the one that comes back has been uniqued/ordered correctly (its the 11-14 one from my example). 

Let me know if that analysis makes sense or I'm missing something here ... if it's a bug I'll take a stab at resolving.

Very good catch!

I guess we could remove the `select` and rewrite the `pluck` as follows:
```ruby
@last_used_at_by_app = Doorkeeper::AccessToken
                           .where(resource_owner_id: current_resource_owner.id)
                           .where.not(last_used_at: nil)
                           .order(application_id: :desc, last_used_at: :desc)
                           .pluck(Arel.sql('DISTINCT ON (application_id) application_id, last_used_at'))
                           .to_h
```

Cool, thanks for confirming -- will attempt to fix, and may move this logic elsewhere in the process (it feels weird to add a controller spec or view spec for this ... maybe move to method on user or something to test)
